claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you with your Child Benefit eligibility assessment, I need to start with some information about your child or children.

**First, I need to understand your situation:**

How old is the child (or children) you're claiming or planning to claim for?

Please let me know:
- **The child's age** (or all children's ages if you have more than one)
- **Their names** (this will help me track their individual eligibility)

The age is important because there are different rules for:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **16 to 19 years old** (may have different requirements)
- **20 years old and over** (different eligibility criteria)

Please provide these details and I'll guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit and wondering if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who's 4 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 4 years old, which means he falls into the "under 16" category. This is good news as children under 16 automatically qualify on the basis of age.

Now let me continue with the assessment to check other eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question about Alex:**

Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?

(Since Alex is only 4 years old, I'm assuming he's not working, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 4!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes sense - Alex is 4 years old, so of course he's not working. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question:**

Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right, such as:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(Again, at 4 years old, I'd expect he's not receiving these, but I need to confirm for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question:**

Is Alex in an apprenticeship?

(Again, at 4 years old, this is unlikely, but I need to confirm - the rules state that most apprenticeships are disqualifying, though Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales are approved.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship - he's only 4 years old!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now let's check your residency situation:**

This is an important part of the eligibility assessment. Child Benefit has specific residency requirements. You need to meet at least one of the following criteria:

1. **Normally live in the UK** - This is the most common path
2. **Settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **Pre-settled status** with additional requirements (working, job-seeking, sufficient resources, studying, or family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

**Which of these applies to your situation?** 

Are you:
- Normally resident in the UK, OR
- Do you have settled/pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, OR
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

Please let me know your residency status so I can proceed with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the straightforward path. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question - Responsibility for Alex:**

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you need to be responsible for the child. This means you either:

1. **Live with the child** - You live under the same roof with Alex
2. **Contribute to their upkeep** - You pay towards their care (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc.) at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount
3. **Pay maintenance** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement

**Which applies to your situation?** Are you living with Alex, or are you contributing to his upkeep in another way?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you're living with Alex. Let me continue with the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question:**

Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied for it?

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child at any given time. Please let me know:
- Is anyone else (such as Alex's other parent, grandparent, or other family member) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
- Or is there any dispute about who should be claiming?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question about Alex's living situation:**

Is Alex in any special circumstances, or is he living with you normally at home?

Specifically, is Alex:
- In hospital
- In care (residential care)
- Being fostered
- Or living normally with you at home

Please let me know his current situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex has been in care for a little while now - just a few weeks. But he still lives with me otherwise.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. So Alex is in care, but it's been only a few weeks. Let me check the specific rules about children in care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question about Alex's care arrangement:**

Since Alex has been in care for a few weeks, I need to check the specific rules. Child Benefit can continue during this period if:

1. **Alex has been in care for 8 weeks or less** (which appears to be your situation - a few weeks), OR
2. **Alex spends at least 24 hours per week at home with you**

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex has been in care for "a few weeks" - this sounds like it's within the 8-week window

**Can you confirm:**
- Exactly how many weeks has Alex been in care? (Is it definitely 8 weeks or less?)
- Does Alex spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you, or does he stay in the care facility most of the time?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been exactly 4 weeks that he's been in care. He doesn't come home during the week - he stays at the care facility full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Since Alex has been in care for exactly 4 weeks (which is well within the 8-week limit), you can continue to claim Child Benefit for him during this period. Let me continue with the final checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question:**

Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he's in care?

In other words:
- Is the council paying for his care and accommodation, OR
- Are you or someone else paying for it privately?

This is the final check needed to determine your eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: The council is not paying for Alex's care - I'm covering the costs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's all the information I need. Let me now provide you with your eligibility determination.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!**

### Summary for Alex (age 4):

**Result:** ELIGIBLE

**Why you qualify:**
- ✅ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✅ He is not working or receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You are responsible for him (he lives with you)
- ✅ No one else is claiming for him
- ✅ Although Alex is currently in care, he has only been there 4 weeks (within the 8-week allowance period)
- ✅ You are personally covering the costs, not the local council

### Important Notes:

**Regarding Alex's care placement:** You can continue claiming Child Benefit for up to 8 weeks while Alex is in care. Since he's only been there 4 weeks, you still have 4 weeks of entitlement remaining. If his care placement extends beyond 8 weeks, you may need to stop claiming unless his circumstances change (e.g., he spends at least 24 hours per week at home with you, or 2 consecutive nights per week at home).

### Next Steps:

1. **If you haven't already applied**, you can claim Child Benefit at: **www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim**
2. Keep records of any care costs you're paying
3. Notify HMRC if Alex's circumstances change (e.g., if he leaves care earlier or his placement extends significantly)

**Reference:** [UK Child Benefit Eligibility](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit claim?
